:::{#lem-surprisal-chain-rule-reversed}
#### Chain rule for surprisal with the conditioning reversed

For [discrete random variables](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv) $X$ and $Y$
and [outcomes](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-experiment-outcome) $x$ and $y$ with $\P(X=x, Y=y) > 0$,

$$\surprisalf{x, y} = \surprisalf{x \mid y} + \surprisalf{y}.$$

:::

::: {.proof}

Applying @thm-surprisal-chain-rule with the roles of $X$ and $Y$ swapped gives

$$\surprisalf{y, x} = \surprisalf{y} + \surprisalf{x \mid y}.$$

The joint event $\{Y=y, X=x\}$ is the event $\{X=x, Y=y\}$,
so $\surprisalf{y, x} = \surprisalf{x, y}$.
Substituting this into the display above,
and reordering the two terms on the right, gives the claim.

:::
